RHODE ISLAND STATEOf HOPE advisory opinion

WHAT IS AN ADVISORY OPINION? An advisory opinion is a legal interpretation of the Rhode Island Code of Ethics issued by the Ethics Commission which provides specific guidance about a particular and impending circumstance. Advisory opinions are based upon the representations made by, or on behalf of, the persons or entities requesting them, and are not the result of adversarial or investigative proceedings.

WHO CAN REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? A person subject to the Code of Ethics may request an advisory opinion about a particular provision of the Code which may affect him or her. WHEN SHOULD I REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? If you believe you may face a real or potential conflict of interest, the time to request an advisory opinion is before you take any official action.

HOW DO I REQUEST AN ADVISORY OPINION? To request an advisory opinion, you must either mail or hand-deliver to the Commission a letter containing your original signature and the following information: • Your name, official position, and a description of your duties; • Your daytime telephone number and e-mail address; • Briefly, the name, jurisdiction and powers of your agency, commission, or office; • The nature of the potential conflict; • A summary of relevant facts; and • Any time constraints.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER I SUBMIT MY REQUEST? ► Letter confirming receipt ► Draft recommendation prepared by staff attorney ► You are strongly encouraged to attend hearing ► Affirmative vote of 5 of 9 Commissioners required ► You will receive written copy ► Also available on Ethics Commission website ► Advisory Opinion and request are public records

Who is required to file? ► All state and municipal elected officials ► Candidates for state or municipal elected office ► All state and some municipal appointed officials ► Some public employees who hold major decision- making positions
All officials required to file must continue to file Financial Disclosure Statements until they have been out of office for one full calendar year.
When must the statement be filed? The Code of Ethics requires that a Financial Disclosure Statement be filed with the Ethics Commission by the last Friday in April . . .
or . . . within (30) days of: ► appointment to a public position; ► the deadline for filing candidacy for public office; or ► the filing of a Notice of Organization with the Board of Elections.

What is the purpose of financial disclosure? ► helps ensure that those people who are acting in the public interest do not use their public positions to further their private financial interests ► provides evidence that there are no conflicts between an official’s financial interests and his or her public office

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically on July 1st. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? There are 5 levels of approval. They are: 1. University of Rhode Island ‐ Facilities Committee (April & May) 2. University of Rhode Island ‐ Senior Leadership (May & June) 3. University of Rhode Island ‐ Board of Trustees (June) 4. Executive Branch 1. Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July‐December) 2. Final Approval by Governor’s Office (Third week of January) 5. Legislative Branch 1. Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) 2. Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and, total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 25% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.
